newsitem.title: USA: Navistar to close foundry, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Navistar to close foundry, take charge.

text.p: Navistar International Corp. will close its Indianapolis Casting Corp. foundry, which employs 650 people, late next year following union rejection of a company proposal, the truck maker said Tuesday.
The move followed the ratification of an extension of Navistar's master contract by 63 percent of voting United Auto Workers union members, announced late Sunday by Navistar.
But UAW members at the Indianapolis plant rejected a proposal the Chicago-based company said "would have kept the foundry cost-competitive and financially viable in the face of foreign competition."

As a result, Navistar said it would proceed with plans to close the Indianapolis Casting Corp., or ICC, plant in late 1998. The company said it has invested heavily at the foundry in recent years, making it more productive and efficient.

"With wage levels 50 percent higher than the competition's, however, ICC could no longer stay competitive without a new labor agreement, particularly in the face of future competition from foundries in Latin America, where labor costs are significantly lower," Navistar said.
The foundry's 650 employees make grey-iron castings for engines, Navistar said.
Navistar said it would take an unspecified charge stemming from the closing in the fourth quarter.
The contract extension takes effect immediately and runs through Oct. 1, 2002, Chicago-based Navistar said.
"We are well on the road to renewal, and this contract is a major milestone," Navistar Chief Executive John Horne said in a statement.

UAW International Vice President Jack Laskowski said in the statement, "I am very pleased with the positive vote on the master contract, and with the work done in Springfield to create a brighter future there. I only wish we had the same success in Indianapolis."
The UAW represents about 8,000 employees in Indianapolis; Springfield, Ohio; Fort Wayne, Ind.; Melrose Park, Ill.; and other locations, the company said.
Navistar stock climbed 81 cents to $22.81 in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
